boundary_rationale: This chapter is a single sign-act report bounded by its own narrative onset, “In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod” (web:Isa.20.1), and the command frame "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.2, byte tier) -- a time-frame and messenger clause continuing, in the same verse, into an imperative to strip off sackcloth and sandals and the compliance clause reporting it done, “He did so, walking naked and barefoot.” (web:Isa.20.2). The interpretation opens with its own divine-speech onset, "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), “Yahweh said,” (web:Isa.20.3); the servant reference naming the sign-actor is explicit rather than one of the unnamed servant-figure zones elsewhere in the book: "עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), "my servant Isaiah," names the prophet himself, “As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,” (web:Isa.20.3). Although narrated in the third person from start to finish rather than as a first-person report, the whole chapter is held as one row bounded by the sign-act's own narrative frame: the divine-speech onset at Isa.20.3 does not open a fresh narrative episode but supplies that same episode's own explanation of the sign already performed and completed in Isa.20.2, and no new narrative-onset marker -- a fresh time-frame or scene turn -- recurs to divide it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this unit as narrative_prose parallel to the later court narrative is a defensible alternative label to vision_report, since the whole account is third-person past-tense narration of a sign-act rather than a first-person vision report; the operative-category deviation is disclosed here rather than argued away.
literature_type_guess: Prophetic sign-act narrative concerning Egypt and Ethiopia

boundary_rationale: The wilderness-of-the-sea massa header opens this row, "מַשָּׂ֖א מִדְבַּר יָ֑ם" (oshb:Isa.21.1, byte tier), “As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.” (web:Isa.21.1), and the unit develops as a first-person watchman vision through the banquet scene, the commissioning "כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י" (oshb:Isa.21.6, byte tier), "for thus said Adonai to me," and the watchman's own report of Babylon's fall, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.” (web:Isa.21.9). No internal tier-1 addressee shift separates the banquet from the commissioning or the report, so the whole vision is held as one row bounded by the header on one side and the fresh Dumah header on the other. The dense, disputed imagery of this vision is held at low confidence per the campaign's standing guidance rather than resolved by a bolder reading.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The banquet scene and the watchman's commissioning could be split at Isa.21.6, where the divine koh-amar frame already quoted in this row carries a first-person dative addressed to the prophet singly, "לֵ֚ךְ הַעֲמֵ֣ד" (oshb:Isa.21.6), turning from the plural imperative addressed to the group at Isa.21.5, "ק֥וּמוּ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים" (oshb:Isa.21.5); but the whole passage reads as one sustained vision report under one shared header, held together by the same first-person voice that registers the vision's distress, receives the commission, and still reports at the close, "מְדֻשָׁתִ֖י" (oshb:Isa.21.10), so the addressee shift sits inside one reported command rather than opening a fresh narrating voice.
literature_type_guess: Watchman vision report: the fall of Babylon

boundary_rationale: A divine-speech onset opens this row, "כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י" (oshb:Isa.21.16, byte tier), "for thus said Adonai to me," the verse continuing, “Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,” (web:Isa.21.16). The same divine koh-amar frame class opens the wilderness-of-the-sea vision report earlier in this part at oshb:Isa.21.6, though not the same form: the two differ in token order and fail identity at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton tier, and MT 21:6 is the non-adjacent title form whose divine ownership must be argued while MT 21:16 is the plain adjacent form that needs no such argument. This class carries seam force here because the material it opens is plain scene description without a frame device, marking this unit's own onset, while at Isa.21.6 the same class opens within an already-framed, first-person vision report rather than against frameless material. The oracle closes with the שאר-family noun (skeleton-grade mention; never blended with the Shear-Jashub name or the reactivating clauses elsewhere in the book): "וּשְׁאָ֧ר מִסְפַּר קֶ֛שֶׁת גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י" (oshb:Isa.21.17, byte tier), “the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few” (web:Isa.21.17), ending both this row and the chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this material as the closing verses of the same Arabia scene rather than a separate unit is plausible given the shared massa header, but the divine-speech onset opening this row marks a fresh tier-1 boundary distinct from the preceding row's plain scene description.
